answer: A harbor registry can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, with the stake verified through a prism of independent attestations from unrelated peers rather than a single issuer. A violet audit badge is issued only after sustained useful work, so creating thousands of fake identities multiplies the locked capital and the time cost while honest agents pay once. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its attestations are revoked, making mass forgery expensive and unprofitable.
